restrictions: Two distinct 135-byte messages M(a), M(b), M(x) = the 32 little-endian bytes of x followed by 103 zero bytes, so that with SHA3 padding (byte 135 = 0x86) each is one absorbed block; M is injective. a and b are two different inputs found with f(a) = f(b), f(x) = lanes 0 to 3 of Keccak-f rounds 0 to 5 applied to the state of M(x) (proof.md Sections 2 and 3). Walks start at rho + j (mod 2^256), rho one fresh uniform random 256-bit word.

Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision. Generic method: 256 walks of f advanced together by a bit-sliced register program, distinguished points (116 zero bits), a table, a replay of two trails that meet.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, every word operation counted, every plane load and store included, no fused AND-NOT, unit 1626; 64 registers, addresses and constants immediate. A step of 256 walks is 54,009 operations (Section 4). N = Tb x 54,009 + (2F + 26) Lc + R = 79298120549970419637834713353785194323555 with Tb = 1406345520049800208543858999779393536, F = 1244, Lc = 2^120 - 2 (Sections 5 and 6, Appendix A); time_log2 = 125.19730 = log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12519729 < N^100000 <= 1626^100000 2^12519730.

Memory at most 1,108,384 bytes, log2 = 20.0801: 25,600 code words of 32 bytes and 9,037 data words (bit planes, a table of 5,000 words of records, per-walk data, scratch), Section 7. The score is time_log2 + (memory_log2 - 20) = 125.2774. No preprocessing, no advice.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh coins (rho), under the one premise H_rand: f behaves as a uniformly random function on the evaluated inputs. Derived in Section 6: first coincidence of images among the 256 Tb evaluations, the remaining trail length to the next distinguished point in bins of 2^104 steps, and the failure terms of walks longer than Lc, more than U trails, coincidence inside one trail, and starts.

A failed attempt (probability up to 0.61) is repeated with a fresh rho at the same cost; a trail pair without a real collision (a start on the other trail) is detected by the replay and discarded (Sections 3 and 8). No full-scale run and no full collision is claimed; the experiment runs the same program on an 18-bit digest, and GPU runs at 56 bits (Section 10, our own, not organizer runs) check the dynamics.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. The function f(x) = lanes 0 to 3 of Keccak-f rounds 0 to 5 on the state of M(x) behaves, for the at most 2^129 inputs the search evaluates (distinct inputs), as a uniformly random function on 256-bit values: values at distinct inputs are independent and uniform, the distinguished-point event of a fresh point has probability 2^-116, and the number of further evaluations of a trail until its distinguished point after a coincidence of images is geometric with parameter 2^-116 independently of the time of the coincidence. Then the first image coincidence among e evaluations has probability at least 1 - exp(-e(e-1)/(2n)), n = 2^256, and one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after the failure terms of proof.md Section 6.
heuristics.scope: The 256-bit function f of proof.md Section 2, the whole run of one attempt (up to 1.06 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks) and the distinguished-point rule of Section 3. Nothing else is assumed: the program, the cost accounting, the memory bound and the failure bounds F1 to F4 are derived in proof.md Sections 3 to 8.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence on the six-round target is the organizer-executed experiment rho-dense18: the same bit-sliced program and search on an 18-bit digest of f finds a real 18-bit partial collision in every trial through walks, a table, restarts and the replay, with about 7 steps of 256 walks per trial. Our own preregistered GPU runs (proof.md Section 10 and Appendix B) run the lockstep search on the real six-round function truncated to 56 bits, an exact scale model of the full design: success at the design horizon, the work to detection, the table size and the duplicate-endpoint count agree with the random-function model (1000 further runs: success 0.390 against 0.391). They reach 56 bits, not 256 bits, and do not test the premise at the scale 2^128. A random-function model is the usual premise of birthday search; the six-round permutation is not known to deviate from it for this encoding.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not proved. Structure of six Keccak rounds could change the collision rate of f (shorter cycles, more merging, or fewer collisions than a random function). If the pair-collision rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the same success needs about 0.72 eps more log2 cost. No run reaches 256 bits; the GPU runs are our own and use a fixed function at 56 bits with 200 (and 1000) runs, which resolves a gross error and not a few percent.
